## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply, or I explain the exception below.
- [x] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)). No `area:*` / `op:*` label covers grouped GEMM, so `mod-cutedsl` is used.

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL (Python/JAX entry points)

## Summary

Follow-up to #1399 and #1535. The grouped quant wrapper, which Transformer Engine's fused MLP uses for FC2 and for the FC1 dgrad, rejected every JAX input. This adds the canonical MXFP8 JAX path, so the MXFP8 MoE forward and backward set (GLU, dGLU, wgrad, quant/dgrad) is complete from JAX on SM100 and Rubin.

- **New entry `cudnn.grouped_gemm_quant_jax_forward`** (jittable, built on `cudnn.jax.call`), dense weights only:
  - A `(m, k)`; B `(experts, n, k)`, or column-wise `(experts, k, n)` with `b_major="n"` (the dFC1 layout from #1422); packed E8M0 scale bytes at any dense rank; optional prob `(m,)`.
  - BF16/FP16 `d_dtype` (default BF16) produces D only. An FP8 `d_dtype` requires `norm_const_tensor` and also produces D_col and the SFD buffers.
  - Returns a `TupleDict` with the eager wrapper's keys; `amax_tensor` is always None. Outputs are not zero-filled.
  - Runs the Rubin quant kernel on SM107 and the SM100 kernel otherwise. The plan cache is keyed by architecture.
- **Wrapper dispatch:** `grouped_gemm_quant_wrapper_sm100` sends JAX inputs with a dense `b_tensor` to it, before the memo.
- **Name:** this is a new public op, so it follows `docs/fe-oss-apis/api_conventions.md` (`<op>_jax_<direction>`, no architecture suffix), unlike its older `*_jax_sm100` siblings. It is reachable from the `cudnn.gemm.cutedsl.grouped` family module only because the lazy-export table and the API index route through it.

## Why

TE's JAX MoE runs GLU and dGLU through cuDNN but the FC1 dgrad through its own grouped GEMM, because no cuDNN JAX path existed for it. After #1422 the quant kernels take canonical layouts, including N-major B, so the JAX adapter passes arrays straight through.

## Related issues

Follow-up to #1275 / #1399 / #1535.

## API and compatibility impact

- One new export: `grouped_gemm_quant_jax_forward` (API index updated).
- `grouped_gemm_quant_wrapper_sm100` with dense MXFP8 JAX inputs now runs instead of raising. It requires `sf_vec_size=32`, and `generate_amax=False` for a BF16/FP16 output (the wrapper default is True; amax is not generated from JAX). Bias, row scale, a caller `d_tensor`, dynamic scheduling, FP4 and `sf_fp8_dtype_override` raise `ValueError` naming the option.
- Discrete (`b_ptrs`) JAX inputs and the `GroupedGemmQuantSm100` class stay rejected, as before. Torch behavior is unchanged.

## Testing

Environment: SM100 (CC 10.0), Python 3.14, JAX 0.11.2, CuTeDSL 4.8.0, torch 2.14.1+cu130, cuDNN 9.24.

- `pytest test/python/gemm/jax test/python/gemm/cutedsl/test_grouped_gemm_quant_canonical.py test/python/gemm/cutedsl/test_grouped_gemm_backward_canonical.py`: **243 passed, 2 xfailed**.
- `pytest test/python/gemm/cutedsl/test_grouped_gemm_quant.py test/python/gemm/cutedsl/test_grouped_gemm_wrapper_memo.py`: **216 passed, 196 skipped**.
- New in `test_grouped_gemm_canonical_jax.py`:
  - `test_canonical_jax_quant_parity`: K- and N-major B, BF16 and FP8 output, with and without prob, 1 and 4 experts, entry and wrapper; eager, jit with command buffers, and an alpha change on the compiled call; byte parity against the Torch wrapper on the same buffers.
  - `test_jax_quant_rejects_unsupported_options`, quant added to the kernel-dispatch test (gated on the DSL's `sm_107a` support) and to the torch-free (`sys.modules["torch"] = None`) jitted run.
- API index runtime check against the editable package: only the GNN native exports differ, which this local cuDNN 9.24 build lacks. `pre-commit` passed on the changed files.
- **Rubin is not hardware-tested:** the Rubin host currently reports no GPU. As a compile-only check on SM100 with `CUTE_DSL_ARCH=sm_107a` and the device family forced to Rubin, all four configurations (K/N-major B x BF16/FP8 output) trace and lower through the Rubin kernel and its adapter branch. No Rubin kernel was executed.
- PR CI's JAX lane uses CuTeDSL 4.6.2, which collection-skips these tests (they need >= 4.7); the 4.7/4.8 JAX lanes run nightly.

nodes.body: Closing: folding this into a single PR that covers the full JAX grouped GEMM matrix.

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `ae0717185f15` against base `db3c367c992f`.

No approval-blocking findings. The canonical JAX adapter preserves the existing quant kernel's layouts and output contract, and the SM100 execution checks below passed. One nonblocking dependency-diagnostic fix is requested for the new SM107 entry. Added this PR to the cuDNN Frontend project; the existing feature/origin/module labels and 1.32.0 milestone are appropriate.

**[P2] Check SM107 DSL capability before importing the Rubin kernel** ([source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/ae0717185f15967e5c7dcaa310550b1a24753962/python/cudnn/gemm/cutedsl/grouped/quant/jax_api.py#L38))

The new route imports the Rubin module as soon as the device family is selected. With a real public DSL 4.7.1 install, which satisfies the general 4.7 floor, selecting this branch raises ImportError for CollectorOp from cutlass.cute.nvgpu.tcgen05. Please run cutedsl_arch_requirement_error((10, 7)) before this import and raise its version/target-specific diagnostic, following python/cudnn/AGENTS.md Rule 7. Add a missing-target regression alongside the current dispatch test, which skips precisely this environment. This is a visible unsupported-environment failure, not a silent numerical issue.

Evidence: Exact-head source with actual DSL 4.7.1: Arch lacks sm_107a; a controlled get_device_type='rubin' call to quant_kernel_type raises ImportError: cannot import name 'CollectorOp'. No unsupported GPU kernel was launched. Attribution: New JAX entry inherits the ungated import pattern used by adjacent routes; this comment concerns the newly added public route.

Validation: Exact-source SM100 quant selection: 26 passed, 116 unrelated cases deselected. Includes Torch/JAX byte parity for eager, JIT and command-buffer calls, K/N-major weights, BF16/FP8 outputs, changing alpha, wrapper dispatch and a Torch-free subprocess. Independent SM100 controls: FP16, BF16 and E5M2 output parity using a 128x256 tile, including warmed eager calls under jax.no_tracing. The suspected 128-wide N-tile gap was disproved: both Torch and JAX reject it before launch. Independent command-buffer probe: 12 executions covering K/N-major weights, BF16/FP8 output, N=384, changed runtime offsets, empty experts and fully empty batches. Active D/D_col rows matched Torch; offset updates reused the compiled function under jax.no_tracing. Attempted native SM107 execution. The existing XLA capability probe rejected this target, so all 26 selected tests skipped. This is explicitly not a Rubin runtime pass. Checked real unsupported DSL behavior separately and reviewed argument ordering, scale-buffer extents, caller-owned offset semantics, cache keys, lazy imports and the unchanged Torch execution body.

Limitations: Rubin JAX execution remains unqualified with the available XLA runtime; the author's compile-only results remain the current adapter evidence for that target. Additional offset probes compare only contractually defined output rows; padding is documented as unspecified. They do not establish end-to-end Transformer Engine training correctness or throughput. There was no previous JAX quant route for a before/after performance comparison. The new branch leaves the Torch kernel and launch path unchanged; warm tracing reuse was checked, but no training performance claim is made. No PR test pipeline was present at publication. The author notes the default JAX lane's older DSL skips these tests; local compatible-runtime results above supply the actual new-path coverage.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.

 **This is an experimental API and subject to change.**
 
+## JAX support
+
+**Canonical MXFP8 (dense weights):** the `jax.jit`-compatible entry point `cudnn.grouped_gemm_quant_jax_forward` takes A `(m, k)`, B `(experts, n, k)` or column-wise `(experts, k, n)` with `b_major="n"` (the dFC1 layout), already MMA-packed E8M0 `sfa_tensor`/`sfb_tensor` bytes (physical or flat; uint8 accepted), int32 `padded_offsets`, fp32 alpha, and an optional prob `(m,)` fp32/bf16. With a BF16/FP16 `d_dtype` (default BF16) it produces D `(m, n)` only. With an FP8 `d_dtype` it requires `norm_const_tensor` `(1,)` and also produces D_col and the physical 6-D SFD buffers; `discrete_col_sfd=True` packs column scales by expert. It returns a `TupleDict` with the eager wrapper's keys; `amax_tensor` is always None. Outputs are not initialized, so rows at or past `padded_offsets[-1]` are unspecified, as in the Torch path. It runs the Rubin quant kernel on SM107 and the SM100 kernel otherwise. `grouped_gemm_quant_wrapper_sm100` dispatches JAX inputs with a dense `b_tensor` to it; set `sf_vec_size=32`, and `generate_amax=False` for a BF16/FP16 output. Bias, row scale, a caller-provided `d_tensor`, dynamic scheduling, FP4, and `sf_fp8_dtype_override` raise `ValueError`. Discrete (`b_ptrs`) weights and the `GroupedGemmQuantSm100` class stay torch-only.
+
 ## Overview
 
 **Unified Grouped GEMM + Quant fusion**: A block-scaled grouped GEMM with output quantization and per-row gating on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs (SM100+), designed for MoE (Mixture of Experts) workloads. Implemented with CUTLASS/CUTE.

+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""JAX-native (XLA custom call) entry point for grouped GEMM quant, built on
+:func:`cudnn.jax.call`.
+
+``grouped_gemm_quant_jax_forward`` is the canonical MXFP8 grouped GEMM with dense
+weights: A ``(m, k)``, B ``(experts, n, k)`` or column-wise ``(experts, k, n)``, and
+already MMA-packed scale bytes, running the SM100 or Rubin (SM107) block-scaled
+quant kernel. ``padded_offsets`` values cannot be host-validated under tracing;
+malformed offsets are the caller's responsibility here (the eager wrapper
+validates them).
+"""
+
+import math
+import os
+
+import cutlass
+import cutlass.cute as cute
+import cutlass.utils
+from cutlass.cute.nvgpu import OperandMajorMode
+
+from cudnn.api_base import TupleDict, ceil_div, get_device_type
+from cudnn.datatypes import _convert_to_cutlass_data_type
+from cudnn.tensor_adapter import detect_framework, get_compute_capability
+from ..canonical_jax import grouped_call, output_type, sf_array, sf_shape
+from ..moe_utils import MoEWeightMode
+from .grouped_gemm_quant import BlockScaledMoEGroupedGemmQuantKernel
+
+kernel_cache = {}
+validated_configs = set()
+
+fp8_dtypes = (cutlass.Float8E4M3FN, cutlass.Float8E5M2)
+
+
+def quant_kernel_type():
+    if get_device_type() == "rubin":
+        from .moe_blockscaled_grouped_gemm_quant_rubin import BlockScaledMoEGroupedGemmQuantKernel as RubinKernel
+
+        return RubinKernel
+    return BlockScaledMoEGroupedGemmQuantKernel
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def grouped_quant_adapter(stream, a, b, sfa, sfb, padded_offsets, alpha, *rest, kernel, mac, rubin, n_major, has_prob, low_precision):
+    # rest: [prob], [norm_const], d, [d_col, sfd_row, sfd_col]
+    prob = rest[0] if cutlass.const_expr(has_prob) else None
+    outputs = rest[int(has_prob) + int(low_precision) :]
+    norm_const = rest[int(has_prob)] if cutlass.const_expr(low_precision) else None
+    d = outputs[0]
+    # The kernel always builds the D_col store descriptor; without quantization it is D, as in the torch path.
+    d_col = outputs[1] if cutlass.const_expr(low_precision) else d
+    sfd_row = outputs[2] if cutlass.const_expr(low_precision) else None
+    sfd_col = outputs[3] if cutlass.const_expr(low_precision) else None
+    b_major_mode = OperandMajorMode.MN if cutlass.const_expr(n_major) else OperandMajorMode.K
+    workspace_ptr = cute.make_ptr(cutlass.Uint8, 0, cute.AddressSpace.gmem, assumed_align=128)
+    if cutlass.const_expr(rubin):
+        kernel(
+            a=a,
+            b=b,
+            sfb=sfb,
+            n=cutlass.Int32(0),
+            k=cutlass.Int32(0),
+            b_stride_size=cutlass.Int64(0),
+            b_major_mode=b_major_mode,
+            workspace_ptr=workspace_ptr,
+            c=d,
+            d=d,
+            d_col=d_col,
+            sfa=sfa,
+            sfd_row_tensor=sfd_row,
+            sfd_col_tensor=sfd_col,
+            amax_tensor=None,
+            norm_const_tensor=norm_const,
+            padded_offsets=padded_offsets,
+            alpha=alpha,
+            bias=None,
+            prob=prob,
+            max_active_clusters=mac,
+            stream=stream,
+        )
+    else:
+        kernel(
+            a=a,
+            b=b,
+            sfb=sfb,
+            n=cutlass.Int32(0),
+            k=cutlass.Int32(0),
+            b_stride_size=cutlass.Int64(0),
+            b_major_mode=b_major_mode,
+            workspace_ptr=workspace_ptr,
+            d=d,
+            d_col=d_col,
+            sfa=sfa,
+            sfd_row_tensor=sfd_row,
+            sfd_col_tensor=sfd_col,
+            amax_tensor=None,
+            norm_const_tensor=norm_const,
+            padded_offsets=padded_offsets,
+            alpha=alpha,
+            row_scale=None,
+            bias=None,
+            prob=prob,
+            max_active_clusters=mac,
+            stream=stream,
+        )
+
+
+def quant_plan(inputs, d, b_major, mma_tiler_mn, cluster_shape_mn, discrete_col_sfd):
+    a, b = inputs["a"], inputs["b"]
+    if b_major not in ("k", "n"):
+        raise ValueError(f"b_major must be 'k' or 'n', got {b_major!r}")
+    if a.ndim != 2 or b.ndim != 3:
+        raise ValueError("JAX requires canonical A (m,k) and B (experts,n,k), or (experts,k,n) with b_major='n'")
+    m, k = a.shape
+    experts = b.shape[0]
+    n, b_k = (b.shape[2], b.shape[1]) if b_major == "n" else b.shape[1:]
+    if m <= 0 or experts <= 0 or k != b_k:
+        raise ValueError("Expected nonempty A/B with matching K and at least one expert")
+    if m % 256:
+        raise ValueError("A rows must be padded to a multiple of 256")
+    ab_dtype = _convert_to_cutlass_data_type(a.dtype)
+    if ab_dtype not in fp8_dtypes or _convert_to_cutlass_data_type(b.dtype) is not ab_dtype:
+        raise ValueError("A and B must have the same MXFP8 dtype, e4m3 or e5m2; packed FP4 is unsupported")
+    for name in ("sfa", "sfb"):
+        if _convert_to_cutlass_data_type(inputs[name].dtype) is not cutlass.Float8E8M0FNU:
+            raise ValueError(f"{name} must contain E8M0 scale bytes")
+    for name, shape in (("alpha", (experts,)), ("norm_const", (1,))):
+        if name in inputs and (tuple(inputs[name].shape) != shape or _convert_to_cutlass_data_type(inputs[name].dtype) is not cutlass.Float32):
+            raise ValueError(f"{name} must have shape {shape} and dtype float32")
+    if "prob" in inputs and (inputs["prob"].shape != (m,) or _convert_to_cutlass_data_type(inputs["prob"].dtype) not in (cutlass.Float32, cutlass.BFloat16)):
+        raise ValueError("prob must have shape (m,) and dtype float32 or bfloat16")
+    if inputs["padded_offsets"].shape != (experts,) or _convert_to_cutlass_data_type(inputs["padded_offsets"].dtype) is not cutlass.Int32:
+        raise ValueError("padded_offsets must have shape (experts,) and dtype int32")
+    d_dtype = _convert_to_cutlass_data_type(d.dtype)
+    low_precision = d_dtype in fp8_dtypes
+    use_2cta_instrs = mma_tiler_mn[0] == 256
+    cluster_shape_mn = tuple(cluster_shape_mn or ((2, 1) if use_2cta_instrs else (1, 1)))
+    margin = int(os.getenv("CUDNNFE_CLUSTER_OVERLAP_MARGIN", "0"))
+    config = (get_device_type(), experts, tuple(mma_tiler_mn), cluster_shape_mn, margin, discrete_col_sfd, low_precision)
+    validation_key = (config, b_major, str(d.dtype), tuple((name, tuple(t.shape), str(t.dtype)) for name, t in inputs.items()))
+    if validation_key not in validated_configs:
+        rest_k = ceil_div(ceil_div(k, 32), 4)
+        for name, rows, groups in (("sfa", m, 1), ("sfb", n, experts)):
+            if math.prod(inputs[name].shape) != 512 * ceil_div(rows, 128) * rest_k * groups:
+                raise ValueError(f"{name.upper()} must contain the complete MMA-packed scale buffer")
+        if experts > 1024:
+            raise ValueError(f"expert count must be <= 1024, got {experts}")
+        kernel_type = quant_kernel_type()
+        # can_implement models K-major B only; column-wise B additionally needs a 16-byte row stride.
+        if (b_major == "n" and n % 16) or not kernel_type.can_implement(
+            ab_dtype,
+            cutlass.Float8E8M0FNU,
+            32,
+            cutlass.Float32,
+            d_dtype,
+            use_2cta_instrs,
+            tuple(mma_tiler_mn),
+            cluster_shape_mn,
+            m,
+            n,
+            k,
+            experts,
+            "k",
+            "k",
+            "n",
+            kernel_type.FIX_PAD_SIZE,
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("Unsupported grouped GEMM quant dtype, tile, cluster, alignment, or layout configuration")
+        validated_configs.add(validation_key)
+    if config not in kernel_cache:
+        major, minor = get_compute_capability()
+        if major * 10 + minor < 100:
+            raise RuntimeError(f"Grouped GEMM quant requires SM100+ compute capability, but found SM{major}{minor}")
+        mac = cutlass.utils.HardwareInfo().get_max_active_clusters(cluster_shape_mn[0] * cluster_shape_mn[1]) - margin
+        if mac <= 0:
+            raise ValueError("CUDNNFE_CLUSTER_OVERLAP_MARGIN leaves no active clusters")
+        kernel = quant_kernel_type()(
+            sf_vec_size=32,
+            acc_dtype=cutlass.Float32,
+            use_2cta_instrs=use_2cta_instrs,
+            mma_tiler_mn=tuple(mma_tiler_mn),
+            cluster_shape_mn=cluster_shape_mn,
+            vectorized_f32=False,
+            generate_sfd=low_precision,
+            discrete_col_sfd=discrete_col_sfd,
+            enable_bias=False,
+            expert_cnt=experts,
+            weight_mode=MoEWeightMode.DENSE,
+            **({"generate_c": False} if get_device_type() == "rubin" else {}),
+        )
+        kernel_cache[config] = (kernel, mac)
+    return kernel_cache[config]
+
+
+def grouped_gemm_quant_jax_forward(
+    a_tensor,
+    b_tensor,
+    sfa_tensor,
+    sfb_tensor,
+    padded_offsets,
+    alpha_tensor,
+    prob_tensor=None,
+    norm_const_tensor=None,
+    *,
+    d_dtype=cutlass.BFloat16,
+    b_major="k",
+    mma_tiler_mn=(256, 256),
+    cluster_shape_mn=None,
+    discrete_col_sfd=False,
+):
+    """Canonical MXFP8 grouped GEMM with optional output quantization, eagerly or under jax.jit.
+
+    A (m,k), dense B (experts,n,k) or column-wise (experts,k,n) with
+    ``b_major="n"``, explicit alpha (experts,) fp32, int32 padded_offsets
+    (experts,), and optional prob (m,) fp32/bf16. Offsets must be nondecreasing
+    multiples of 256 within [0,m]; m is padded to 256. SF buffers contain packed
+    E8M0 MMA-tiled bytes, at any dense rank (uint8 bit patterns also accepted).
+    With a BF16/FP16 ``d_dtype`` only D (m,n) is produced. With an FP8
+    ``d_dtype``, norm_const (1,) fp32 is required and D, D_col and the physical
+    6-D SFD buffers are produced; ``discrete_col_sfd=True`` packs column scales
+    by expert. Returns a TupleDict with the eager wrapper's keys; amax is not
+    generated. Outputs are not initialized, so rows at or past
+    padded_offsets[-1] are unspecified, as in the torch path. Runs the Rubin
+    quant kernel on SM107 and the SM100 kernel otherwise.
+    """
+    d_dtype = _convert_to_cutlass_data_type(d_dtype)
+    low_precision = d_dtype in fp8_dtypes
+    if low_precision and norm_const_tensor is None:
+        raise ValueError("norm_const_tensor is required when FP8 inputs are used with FP8 output")
+    inputs = dict(a=a_tensor, b=b_tensor, sfa=sfa_tensor, sfb=sfb_tensor, padded_offsets=padded_offsets, alpha=alpha_tensor)
+    if prob_tensor is not None:
+        inputs["prob"] = prob_tensor
+    if low_precision:
+        inputs["norm_const"] = norm_const_tensor
+    for name, tensor in inputs.items():
+        argument = name if name == "padded_offsets" else f"{name}_tensor"
+        if tensor is None:
+            raise ValueError(f"{argument} is required for the JAX MXFP8 path")
+        if detect_framework(tensor) != "jax":
+            raise ValueError(f"{argument} must be a JAX array or tracer")
+    inputs["sfa"] = sf_array(sfa_tensor)
+    inputs["sfb"] = sf_array(sfb_tensor)
+    m = a_tensor.shape[0]
+    n = b_tensor.shape[-1 if b_major == "n" else -2]
+    outputs = dict(d=output_type((m, n), d_dtype))
+    if low_precision:
+        outputs.update(
+            d_col=output_type((m, n), d_dtype),
+            sfd_row=output_type(sf_shape(m, n), cutlass.Float8E8M0FNU),
+            sfd_col=output_type(sf_shape(n, m), cutlass.Float8E8M0FNU),
+        )
+    kernel, mac = quant_plan(inputs, outputs["d"], b_major, mma_tiler_mn, cluster_shape_mn, discrete_col_sfd)
+    result = grouped_call(
+        grouped_quant_adapter,
+        kernel,
+        mac,
+        tuple(output_type(t.shape, t.dtype) for t in inputs.values()),
+        tuple(outputs.values()),
+        zero_dprob=False,
+        rubin=get_device_type() == "rubin",
+        n_major=b_major == "n",
+        has_prob=prob_tensor is not None,
+        low_precision=low_precision,
+    )(*inputs.values())
+    return TupleDict(
+        d_tensor=result[0],
+        d_col_tensor=result[1] if low_precision else None,
+        amax_tensor=None,
+        sfd_row_tensor=result[2] if low_precision else None,
+        sfd_col_tensor=result[3] if low_precision else None,
+    )

reviews.body:
**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `ae0717185f15` against base `db3c367c992f`.

No approval-blocking findings. The canonical JAX adapter preserves the existing quant kernel's layouts and output contract, and the SM100 execution checks below passed. One nonblocking dependency-diagnostic fix is requested for the new SM107 entry. Added this PR to the cuDNN Frontend project; the existing feature/origin/module labels and 1.32.0 milestone are appropriate.

**[P2] Check SM107 DSL capability before importing the Rubin kernel** ([source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/ae0717185f15967e5c7dcaa310550b1a24753962/python/cudnn/gemm/cutedsl/grouped/quant/jax_api.py#L38))

The new route imports the Rubin module as soon as the device family is selected. With a real public DSL 4.7.1 install, which satisfies the general 4.7 floor, selecting this branch raises ImportError for CollectorOp from cutlass.cute.nvgpu.tcgen05. Please run cutedsl_arch_requirement_error((10, 7)) before this import and raise its version/target-specific diagnostic, following python/cudnn/AGENTS.md Rule 7. Add a missing-target regression alongside the current dispatch test, which skips precisely this environment. This is a visible unsupported-environment failure, not a silent numerical issue.

Evidence: Exact-head source with actual DSL 4.7.1: Arch lacks sm_107a; a controlled get_device_type='rubin' call to quant_kernel_type raises ImportError: cannot import name 'CollectorOp'. No unsupported GPU kernel was launched. Attribution: New JAX entry inherits the ungated import pattern used by adjacent routes; this comment concerns the newly added public route.

Validation: Exact-source SM100 quant selection: 26 passed, 116 unrelated cases deselected. Includes Torch/JAX byte parity for eager, JIT and command-buffer calls, K/N-major weights, BF16/FP8 outputs, changing alpha, wrapper dispatch and a Torch-free subprocess. Independent SM100 controls: FP16, BF16 and E5M2 output parity using a 128x256 tile, including warmed eager calls under jax.no_tracing. The suspected 128-wide N-tile gap was disproved: both Torch and JAX reject it before launch. Independent command-buffer probe: 12 executions covering K/N-major weights, BF16/FP8 output, N=384, changed runtime offsets, empty experts and fully empty batches. Active D/D_col rows matched Torch; offset updates reused the compiled function under jax.no_tracing. Attempted native SM107 execution. The existing XLA capability probe rejected this target, so all 26 selected tests skipped. This is explicitly not a Rubin runtime pass. Checked real unsupported DSL behavior separately and reviewed argument ordering, scale-buffer extents, caller-owned offset semantics, cache keys, lazy imports and the unchanged Torch execution body.

Limitations: Rubin JAX execution remains unqualified with the available XLA runtime; the author's compile-only results remain the current adapter evidence for that target. Additional offset probes compare only contractually defined output rows; padding is documented as unspecified. They do not establish end-to-end Transformer Engine training correctness or throughput. There was no previous JAX quant route for a before/after performance comparison. The new branch leaves the Torch kernel and launch path unchanged; warm tracing reuse was checked, but no training performance claim is made. No PR test pipeline was present at publication. The author notes the default JAX lane's older DSL skips these tests; local compatible-runtime results above supply the actual new-path coverage.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.
